log: No empty or repeated triangles were found.
Flat areas: 5 walls and other flat areas (14666 triangles) pressed onto their planes and lit as one face each. No point moved more than 0.09 percent of the part's size.
Windows: none found. A window has to be set back from its frame in the mesh. Glass that is only painted on a flat wall cannot be told from the wall.
Signs and doors: 2 doors (set back like a window, but painted or reaching the ground) named as material door, unchanged in look.

Walls: 9 walls and 2 roof slopes moved to a 2048 px texture of their own, one rectangle each at one even scale. The old paint was smoothed to its colors (stains, bands and corners stay, thin lines and creases go) and a new stucco surface was laid over it. Material walls. Nothing was moved.
Surfaces are scanned photographs (stucco, roof) laid at true size and tinted to the old paint.

Where a wall is far darker than its own usual color (a window, vent or door that is only painted on, with no step in the mesh) the old paint was kept as it was, so it is not smeared. A solid block of other paint half a meter or more across (a pale window, a brown door) is kept whole the same way and faded into the new wall at its edge.

Walls taken whole: 9784 loose triangles that lay in a wall's plane or reached from it into a painted window joined that wall, so no wedge of old paint is left across it. Where two sheets of a wall lay on each other, the one in front shows.
Roof: each slope is lit as one plane and its tiles come from the texture. The raised tiles of the mesh stay in place, so the eaves keep their shape.
Color standard: every color texture was already inside the shared range. Nothing was changed.
Surface maps: every material already has its own.
Reduced 1290496 triangles to 57890. The surface moved by at most 2.0 percent of the model size. Edges between parts were held in place.
The model was scaled by 3.7639, set on the ground, centered.
Textures: 2 resized to 2048 px or under. Saved 21.3 MB.
